prompt: This is the Zachman grid without its words. Put each question on its column, in the framework's order.
hint: Things, process, places, people, time, motivation.

prompt: Match each Zachman column to a Carcará example.
hint: Inventory, process, distribution, responsibility, timing, motivation.

pairs.right: departures and the São João peak

prompt: How many cells does the Zachman grid have?
What is the most common misreading of Zachman's rows, by the lesson?

choices.text: That they are ordered by importance
choices.why: A misreading of the columns, which have no order, more than of the rows.

choices.text: That each row just adds detail
choices.why: Right: each row is a different description, in a different language, for a different reader.

choices.text: That the rows are teams in the company
choices.why: They are perspectives; one person may work in several.

choices.text: That row 6 is optional
choices.why: Row 6 is the running enterprise; the misreading the lesson names is about detail.

prompt: How does the lesson contrast C4's levels with Zachman's rows?
hint: One zooms; the other changes language.

choices.text: They are the same idea with different names
choices.why: C4 magnifies one kind of description; Zachman's rows are different kinds.

choices.text: C4 has four levels and Zachman six, so Zachman is more detailed
choices.why: The count is not the difference; the nature of the move is.

choices.text: C4 zooms; Zachman's rows translate
choices.why: Yes: a C4 component diagram is a closer look at a container; Zachman's row 4 is a different model from row 2.

choices.text: C4 covers the business row and Zachman does not
choices.why: The reverse: C4 lives roughly in rows 3 and 4.

prompt: A business manager is handed an engineer's container diagram because it is more complete. What is wrong?

choices.text: Fine, as long as it carries a legend
choices.why: A legend explains marks; it does not change the language or the question.

choices.text: The wrong row, in the wrong words
choices.why: Right: it answers questions the manager never asked.

choices.text: Container diagrams carry too much detail for anyone
choices.why: For an engineer they are exactly right.

choices.text: It should be printed larger
choices.why: Size does not change the audience it was written for.

prompt: Why does Zachman call his framework an ontology?

choices.text: It classifies, without steps
choices.why: Yes: it classifies kinds of description and says nothing about steps; there is no starting cell and no process.

choices.text: Because it is written in a formal logic
choices.why: It is a grid with rules, not a formal logic.

choices.text: Because it replaces TOGAF's method
choices.why: It combines with a method such as TOGAF's ADM rather than replacing it.

choices.text: Because it was published in a philosophy journal
choices.why: It appeared in an IBM journal on information systems.

prompt: Lesson 4's activity diagram with swimlanes mixes how and who. What does Zachman's grid say about it?

choices.text: It is invalid and should be split
choices.why: Composites are normal and often necessary; the grid does not forbid them.

choices.text: It is a composite, and the grid names what it mixes
choices.why: Right: when it becomes hard to read, you know which primitive to split out.

choices.text: It belongs in the When column
choices.why: It shows steps and who does them; time is not its subject.

choices.text: It is a primitive of the How column
choices.why: The swimlanes add who, which makes it span two columns.

prompt: Which of these follow from Zachman's framework being an ontology? Choose all that apply.
hint: No steps, no starting point, no verdicts.

choices.text: There is no starting cell
choices.why: Yes: a method would have one.

choices.text: It combines with a method such as TOGAF's ADM
choices.why: Yes: TOGAF for the process, Zachman as the filing system.

choices.text: It finds gaps, and judging them is still yours
choices.why: Yes: whether an empty cell matters is a judgement.

choices.text: Its columns are filled from left to right
choices.why: The columns have no order.

prompt: Match each artefact from this course to its main Zachman cell.
Which gap did placing the course in the grid find in the When column?

choices.text: No picture of Carcará's business calendar
choices.why: Right: São João, Christmas and the monthly close live in people's heads.

choices.text: No sequence diagram of payment
choices.why: Lesson 2 drew one.

choices.text: No state machine of a ticket
choices.why: Lesson 4 drew one.

choices.text: No timeline of decision records
choices.why: Lesson 5 drew one, and it answers why rather than when.

prompt: The grid shows Who · engineer is empty: who runs each container on call. What does the lesson conclude?

choices.text: The course failed to cover operations
choices.why: The lesson calls empty cells scope choices, not failures.

choices.text: On-call rotas are not architecture
choices.why: The lesson argues they belong next to the diagrams.

choices.text: A scope choice that nobody had noticed
choices.why: Yes: the grid turned an unnoticed choice into a noticed one, and lesson 11 argues on-call ownership belongs beside the diagrams.

choices.text: Each of the cells is needed before going live
choices.why: No framework demands all 36; judgement decides which matter.

prompt: Match each framework to the kind of thing it is.
Which habits does the lesson say the frameworks keep repeating in their own words? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Separate the audiences
choices.why: Yes: Zachman's rows, 42010's stakeholders, C4's levels, 4+1's views.

choices.text: Separate why, what, how and with what
choices.why: Yes: Zachman, IAF, TOGAF's building blocks, lesson 6.

choices.text: Trace each decision to its reason
choices.why: Yes: IAF's ordering, TOGAF's requirements, lessons 5 and 6.

choices.text: Prefer one notation for each audience alike
choices.why: The opposite: different readers need different pictures.

prompt: A new framework is proposed to you. Which three questions does the lesson suggest asking?

choices.text: Its price, vendor and certification
choices.why: Practical, and they do not tell you what the framework is.

choices.text: Its kind, its scale and its one idea
choices.why: Right: they place it among the others quickly.

choices.text: Its age, its popularity, its tools
choices.why: None of these says what problem it solves.

choices.text: Who wrote it, who uses it, who teaches it
choices.why: Social facts, not what the framework is.

prompt: By the lesson, what do framework names on a CV do, and what gets the job?

choices.text: Names get the CV read; habits get the job
choices.why: Yes: interviews test situations, not the framework's content.

choices.text: Names get the job; habits are learnt after
choices.why: Interviewers ask situational questions that only the habits answer.

choices.text: Certificates get the job; names are decoration
choices.why: Certificates are usually desirable, not decisive.

choices.text: Neither matters; experience alone does
choices.why: The lesson says both have a role.

prompt: An interviewer says: draw the architecture of a system you worked on. What are they watching for, by the lesson?

choices.text: How fast you draw
choices.why: Speed is not the skill.

choices.text: Whether you know UML symbols by heart
choices.why: Notation helps, and it is not what the question tests first.

choices.text: Whether you use the company's preferred tool
choices.why: On a whiteboard, there is no tool.

choices.text: Question, audience and notation, named first
choices.why: Right: lessons 1 to 4, applied under pressure.

prompt: A team argues whether to adopt Zachman or TOGAF. What is the lesson's answer?

choices.text: Zachman, because it is older and more complete
choices.why: Age and completeness do not make an ontology a method.

choices.text: TOGAF, because Zachman has no steps
choices.why: True of Zachman, and a reason to use it beside a method, not instead of it.

choices.text: An ontology and a method combine
choices.why: Yes: many teams run TOGAF and file its outputs in Zachman's cells.

choices.text: Neither; use C4
choices.why: C4 is for one system; the argument here is about the enterprise.

prompt: Zachman calls his framework an ___: a classification of what kinds of description exist, not a method.
